title: Signs in the horizons and in themselves
hookLine: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves (41:53)
carry: signs out there, signs in here

lines: A WIDE VIEW: YOU GET SMALL.
cards: Stand at the edge of a wide view, a coastline, a desert, a city at night from a high window, and you can feel yourself get small.
Now close your eyes and feel your heartbeat, the breath going in and out without your asking, the strange fact that you're aware of any of it. That gets large in a different way.
Two directions to look: out, as far as the eye goes, and in, as deep as you can go. One verse before its last, Surah Fussilat points both ways at once.

teach.b: Verse fifty-three. Pickthall: "We shall show them Our portents on the horizons and within themselves until it will be manifest unto them that it is the Truth." Portents, in Pickthall's English, is the Arabic ayat, signs.
And ayat is also the word for the verses of the Qur'an. A verse is a sign. A sunset is a sign.
Your own heartbeat is a sign. One word covers all three. Then the two places.
Al-afaq, the horizons: the far edges of the world.
And anfusihim, themselves: the inner world, the body, the mind, the soul. The signs keep being shown, in both directions, until it becomes clear that this is the truth. What exactly are these signs?
Commentators differ. Some early scholars read the horizons as the lands that would open to the Muslims, and the selves as events in Mecca itself: history as a sign.

Many later scholars read it as the cosmos and the human being: nature as a sign. The verse holds both. Surah adh-Dhariyat says something similar: in the earth are signs for the certain, and in yourselves; do you not see?
And the verse ends with a question: isn't it enough that your Lord is witness over everything? So the signs aren't a puzzle to be solved once.
They're shown, again and again, to anyone looking: out at the horizon, in at the heartbeat, and down at the page.

how: Muslims practice tafakkur, reflection on creation and on the self, as a form of worship, and use the same word, ayah, for a verse of the Qur'an and a sign in the world.

o: in the mosque and the market.

games.why: al-afaq and anfusihim: the far edges of the world and the inner self, until the truth becomes clear.

practice: Look out a window if you can, find the farthest thing you can see, a tree line, a rooftop, a cloud, and rest your eyes on it for a few breaths.
Then close your eyes and turn the looking inward: your breath, your heartbeat, the fact that you're noticing at all. Move between the two, slowly, out and in.

wordCard.voice: Ayat, signs, the word that names both the Qur'an's verses and the proofs shown out at the world's horizons and within the self. Today's word.
